videos.t: Building LASER Harp with an Arduino
videos.desc:
Homemade DIY Laser Harp using a 200mW green laser. Using an Arduino Microprocessor to control the laser and galvanometer, we produced 7 beams. Detecting reflected light from whatever breaks the beams we can determine which note to play. The MIDI output is fed into a virtual MIDI synthesizer running on a laptop to produce the sounds. Challenging project, but worth the effort.

videos.t: How We Play Music With Tesla Coils - See It In Action!
videos.desc: These are our twin homemade Tesla Coils. They are  dual resonance solid state Tesla coils which are controlled electronically to produce musical notes. Audio signals in MIDI format are fed into the coil through fiberoptic cables, so they can be played as musical instruments.

videos.t: Watching Radioactive Decay With a Cheap Cloud Chamber
videos.desc: How to build a simple cloud chamber but get great results. Using just a fish tank and some household items we built this simple cloud chamber and tested some radioactive sources.

videos.t: We Converted a Walmart bicycle Into a Speedy E-Bike
videos.desc:
We wanted to see if we could convert a cheap Walmart bicycle into an electric bike and how fast it could go. To do this we had to build a custom Lithium battery pack and drive the bike with a large brushless motor controlled with an arduino. Lots of other mods and endless testing to finally get it working. The results exceeded our expectations.

Motor - Turnigy D5035-125KV Sensored Brushless Motor

videos.t: How We Use High Voltage To Create Unique Lightning Pattern Artwork
videos.desc:
Using high voltage to create Lichtenberg Figures in in wood. We used this technique to create coasters each with original patterns.
WARNING - this project uses very high voltage and should not be attempted.

videos.t: I Got Shot With An Air Cannon!
videos.desc: We decided we needed an air cannon after finding an old compressor tank in the shed out back. By adding a pneumatic cylinder we were able to fire the cannon with the push of a button which is much more efficient than hand opening the valve. Watch the end to see Jason get nailed by it.

videos.t: Just Blowing S#!T Up For Fun With High Voltage
videos.desc:
Blowing up stuff with a high voltage capacitor bank. A set of 6 caps each of 33,000uF discharged through a few components. This is just a fun video of making things go boom. It's amazing the amount of electrical power that can be dumped into an object in milliseconds. Don't try this at home - this thing is danger scary.

videos.t: I Built the Most Stressful Game Ever Made
